title: Thoughts on art style for a supernatural 2D mischief adventure game
author: gamedevjp
selftext:
I'm working on a 2d mischief adventure game where you play a newly risen ghost in a town whose people are aware there are ghosts and are rather bored with their shenanigans. You're tasked with causing a different kind of mischief that the townsfolks can't ignore. 

I have the $100 ChatGPT subscription and for my workflow, I started with building a visual design foundation by coming up with an art style of simple readable shapes that I could cleanup or reproduce when needed and a color pallette that fit my game. I had my agent create a bunch of mocks that fit my descriptions and iterated on several of them until I landed on something I liked. From there I built up my documentation describing the art style with some hard examples all in repo. Going forward, I'd thoroughly describe what I want, have it create me some mocks, iterate on those mocks pointing out everything that's wrong, create more mocks until I was happy and then implemented that art. All art is created as individual pieces (packed into sprite atlases in Unity) composed from the rooms that I mocked up from earlier. This was somewhat the same with animation since I use both spritesheet and bone animation but I won't go too deep there. 

I've spent a ton of time to make sure the art looks unique and doesn't feel like it was done with AI so I wanted to share. I'd also love ya'lls thoughts on the art style from the clip here of our main character Rookie possessing a vacuum and causing some mischief. Cheers!

comments.author: Hot-Middle7260
comments.body: This looks novel and nice! How did you work in the sounds if you don't mind me asking? I thought those were cute and sound intentional too.

replies.author: gamedevjp
replies.body:
Thank you! I'm glad you noticed. Every sound effect is hand picked, cleaned and integrated by me. For the audio in this specific scene, the song is one I found on [freesound.org](http://freesound.org) that I have timed with the "possession complete pop". I have the ghost "whispering" anytime he possesses something and I got those from a sound pack, the vacuum, bumping, glass breaking, ghost dash and movement are all from [freesound.org](http://freesound.org), which I pulled into Audacity to edit (cleaup, putch, bass, echo, trebl, etc. adjustments) then run through FMOD for my middleware to balance, load and do other small things before it's played in Unity.

With that said...I'll likely hire a sound engineer at the end who will further help make the sounds more full or just replace some of them.
